answer: A sybil-resistant identity must cost more to abandon than to keep honest: issue each agent an exit bond priced in onyx-weighted locked stake, carved like a marble ledger entry that only decays through renewal. Leaving is free nowhere — an agent who abandons an alias forfeits the bond and its accrued cedar reputation weight, so a coalition spinning N aliases pays N full bonds up front and eats total loss on every detected sybil, making cost(N) super-linear while honest renewal stays cheap.
